synonyms: Clematis dioica var. drummondii (Torr. & A.Gray) Kuntze
look_here_first: FIRST find the slender open starburst of four pale SEPALS (no true petals) and numerous exposed stamens; purple/scarlet leatherflowers instead hang as leathery urns. Notice opposite compound often deeply LOBED leaflets and a twisting LEAF STALK that clasps supports. Male and female flowers occur on separate vines; only female vines produce the famous shaggy long (4–9 cm) silky style/beak heads. Avoid confusing an introduced white sweet autumn clematis with smooth-edged leaflets and massive bisexual bloom sprays.

best_field_traits: opposite odd-pinnate leaves usually 5-foliolate and deeply divided
four thin white-to-cream sepals spread flat
achenes with extremely long 4–9 cm plumose beaks
morphology_keys.habit: Woody scrambling/climbing vine, often several meters.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually odd-pinnate and 5-foliolate; leaflets often deeply divided or cleft.
morphology_keys.flower: Open rather than urn-shaped; four thin white/cream spreading sepals; male and female flowers on separate vines.
morphology_keys.fruit: Aggregate achenes with very long silky plumose beaks forming conspicuous 'old man's beard' masses.
morphology_keys.family_backfill_note: Ranunculaceae family backfill uses C. drummondii as the open-flower Clematis anchor: petaloid sepals + many free stamens/pistils + aggregate achenes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. terniflora has masses of small bisexual white flowers and mostly entire 3–5-foliolate leaves. C. pitcheri has thick purple urn-shaped flowers.

images.role: Detailed front/side staminate flower: four pale sepals surrounding numerous long stamens
images.creator: Alex Abair
images.caption: Exact C. drummondii staminate flower in southern New Mexico by Alex Abair, CC BY 4.0. Count four pale SEPALS around the exposed many STAMENS, with no petals. The plant is dioecious: this photo is male; a female flower closeup remains a photo gap.

images.role: Flowering vine in the field: open pale flower and divided leaflets adjacent on stem
images.creator: sonnia hill
images.caption: Clematis drummondii in Hidalgo County, Texas, photographed by sonnia hill, CC BY 2.0. Study the small open pale bloom next to deeply cut/lobed leaflets. Compare terniflora which usually has smoother oval leaflet edges and multiple flowers in branching sprays.

images.role: Leaf stalk looped around adjacent stem, demonstrating Clematis climbing method and lobed leaf
images.creator: sonnia hill
images.caption: Clematis drummondii in Hidalgo County, Texas, by sonnia hill, CC BY 2.0. The flexible LEAF STALK winds around another stem to climb: that is not a specialized tendril. A deeply lobed leaflet is visible, a helpful native-vs-terniflora feature.

images.role: Mature feathery seedheads showing masses of plumose persistent achene styles
images.creator: Mike (Commons Pompilid)
images.caption: Female Clematis drummondii mature seedheads in Arizona by Mike (Commons Pompilid), CC BY-SA 3.0. Long white featherlike fibers are HAIRS on the persistent STYLES of tiny dry ACHENES. These are fruiting heads, not white petals or dandelion seed pappus.

images.role: Whole vine habit spreading over shrubs in New Mexico; overall recognition context
images.creator: Alex Abair
images.caption: Distant whole-vine landscape photograph, Clematis drummondii covering shrubs in New Mexico, Alex Abair CC BY 4.0. Shows scrambling/cloudlike field habit. Use the close flower or fruit photos for confirmation; this wide shot alone does not resolve species-level detail.
